title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Assistant Accountant

Salary: £25,000

Location: Leeds

Employment Type: Full-time, Permanent

Working Hours: 37.5 hours per week

About the Company

We are a modern, forward-thinking and cloud-first accountancy practice providing accounting services to a varied portfolio of small businesses, sole traders and limited companies.

Operating in a collaborative, technology-driven environment, the practice places a strong emphasis on employee development, career progression and creating a supportive workplace. With a growing team and a commitment to developing talent, this is an excellent opportunity to join an established and expanding practice.

About the Role

An opportunity has arisen for an Assistant Accountant to join the team, supporting the delivery of bookkeeping, payroll and accounts preparation services to a varied client base.

This role would suit someone with previous accountancy practice experience who has a basic understanding of bookkeeping, payroll and accounts preparation and is keen to develop their technical knowledge and progress their career.

Working alongside experienced accountants, you will gain exposure to a range of accounting duties, receive guidance and training, and gradually take on additional responsibilities as your experience and confidence grow.

The successful candidate will be organised, detail-oriented and motivated to learn, with a genuine interest in developing a long-term career in accountancy.

Key Responsibilities
- Assisting with bookkeeping and maintaining accurate financial records for a range of clients.
- Supporting the preparation of accounts for sole traders and limited companies.
- Assisting with payroll processing and associated administration.
- Processing purchase and sales invoices, bank transactions and financial records.
- Carrying out bank reconciliations and investigating discrepancies.
- Assisting with VAT returns and other routine financial submissions.
- Maintaining accurate client records and ensuring financial information is up to date.
- Liaising with colleagues and clients to obtain missing information and resolve queries.
- Supporting the wider accounting team with day-to-day duties and meeting relevant deadlines.
- Developing technical knowledge across bookkeeping, payroll, accounts preparation and other areas of accountancy.

Experience & Requirements
- Previous experience working within an accountancy practice is essential.
- Practical experience in bookkeeping, payroll and basic accounts preparation.
- A basic understanding of accounting principles and financial processes.
- Good attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate work.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage workloads effectively.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- A proactive approach with a willingness to learn and develop new skills.
- Competent IT skills, with experience using accounting software being advantageous.

Qualifications
- A degree in Accounting, Finance or a related subject would be advantageous but is not essential.
- AAT studies or a willingness to pursue an accounting qualification would be beneficial.
- Candidates with relevant accountancy practice experience and a strong desire to develop their technical skills are encouraged to apply.

Working Pattern & Flexibility
- Working Hours:5 hours per week.
- Flexible Working: Flexible working arrangements may be available following the initial training period, subject to the practice's requirements.
- Hybrid Working: The opportunity to work from home is available following successful completion of the probation period.
- Office Environment: A collaborative and supportive workplace, with opportunities to learn directly from experienced colleagues.

Salary & Benefits
- Salary: Approximately £25,000, depending on experience.
- Annual Leave: 25 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays.
- Study Support: Financial support of up to £500 per exam or module towards eligible AAT, ACCA or CTA studies, reimbursed following successful completion of probation.
- Paid Study Leave: Two paid study days per module, comprising one exam day and one revision day.
- Hybrid Working: The opportunity to work from home following successful completion of probation.
- Career Progression: Clear opportunities to progress into more senior accounting positions as technical knowledge and experience develop.
- Training & Development: Practical, on-the-job training and support from experienced members of the team.
- Company Culture: A friendly, collaborative working environment with a casual dress code.
- Social Events: Regular team and employee-welfare activities, including sports days, coffee mornings and other informal social events.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Our client is seeking a motivated and commercially aware Accounts Assistant to join their finance team, the business is a fast-paced manufacturing company.
This role will focus primarily on purchase ledger activities, ensuring invoices are processed accurately, supplier accounts are maintained correctly and payments are made in line with agreed terms.

Alongside the day-to-day accounts payable responsibilities, you will contribute to month-end activities, account reconciliations and the preparation of financial information to support reporting and audit requirements.

Key Duties of Accounts Assistant
- Manage the day-to-day processing of supplier invoices, credit notes and employee expenses, ensuring transactions are correctly coded and recorded.
- Check invoices against purchase orders and goods received records, investigating and resolving any differences.
- Maintain the purchase ledger, ensuring supplier accounts and financial records remain accurate and up to date.
- Complete regular supplier statement reconciliations and investigate any variances or overdue items.
- Prepare supplier payment proposals and payment runs in line with agreed credit terms and internal procedures.
- Act as a point of contact for supplier enquiries, providing timely responses and resolving queries professionally.
- Work closely with Procurement, Goods In, Production and other relevant teams to address invoice, pricing and delivery discrepancies.
- Review aged creditor balances and take appropriate action to clear outstanding queries.
- Maintain organised financial records and supporting documentation to meet internal control and audit requirements.
- Support the month-end close, including balance sheet reconciliations, accruals and related journals.
- Assist with VAT submissions and other financial reporting activities as required.
- Provide support across the wider finance function, including sales ledger and credit control, to ensure effective team cover.
- Contribute to the ongoing improvement of finance processes, ensuring work is completed efficiently and in accordance with company policies.
- Handle sensitive financial information responsibly, maintaining confidentiality and a consistently high level of accuracy.

Essential:
- AAT qualified
- Strong Excel and finance system knowledge
- Strong attention to detail and comfort working with repetitive, high-volume tasks.
- Willingness to adapt as the team introduces system and process improvements.
- Good communication skills and a proactive approach.

description: A new opportunity has arisen for a medical receptionist to join our team. title: Care Navigator/ Medical Receptionist
description: South Queen Street Medical Centre are looking to appoint a care navigator/ receptionist to join our busy GP practice who will be the first point of contact for patients, contractors, and visitors as well as carrying out general office management tasks. Working pattern 5 hours per day, 5 days a week, alternate weekly am & pm shifts, 8am-630pm. Flexibility and overtime will be required for this role. You will be responsible for the general reception duties within the Practice and work with our established processes, policies, and procedures to provide a comprehensive high-quality service and deal efficiently and courteously with patient enquiries. You will receive, assist, and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. You will provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. You will have excellent communication skills, a compassionate and friendly nature who can operate in a busy environment with a range of people and professions, as you will be working with our clinical and administration teams. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organised and an effective communicator who can provide a professional and warm welcome to our patients, ensuring every contact is of the highest quality. IT skills are essential, as you will be regularly creating searches, data input and monitoring our achievements and progress against national, local, and internal targets. You will also process prescription requests and provide a full administrative service. GCSE grade C or above in English and Maths is essential for this role. Key Duties and Responsibilities Patient Reception and Customer Service Act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Welcome patients in a friendly, respectful and professional manner. Respond to general enquiries and provide accurate information about practice services, opening hours and appointment procedures. Deal sensitively with patients who may be anxious, distressed, frustrated or experiencing difficult personal circumstances. Maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception and waiting area. Manage challenging situations professionally and escalate complaints or concerns to the appropriate member of the practice team. Care Navigation and Appointment Management Handle patient requests for appointments, advice and access to healthcare services by telephone and in person. Use approved care navigation protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician or service, including GPs, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, physiotherapists and other available services where appropriate. Gather relevant non-clinical information to help determine the appropriate appointment pathway, without attempting to diagnose medical conditions. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the practices clinical computer system. Identify potentially urgent concerns in accordance with practice procedures and promptly escalate them to a clinician. Provide information about alternative services, such as NHS 111, where appropriate and in accordance with practice guidance. Maintain accurate records of patient contacts and appointment requests. Telephone and Administrative Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and manage a busy call queue efficiently. Handle patient messages and ensure they are passed to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies and direct medication queries to the appropriate professional. Register new patients and update demographic details, contact information and other relevant records. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and electronic communications. Assist with administrative tasks, including recalling patients for appointments, supporting clinical audits and maintaining accurate practice records. Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow up requests within agreed timescales. Clinical Systems and Data Management Use the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, to access and update patient information. Ensure patient details, appointment information and messages are recorded accurately and promptly. Handle sensitive patient information securely and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, data protection legislation, information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures for accessing, storing and sharing patient information appropriately. Teamwork and Practice Support Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, care coordinators and administrative colleagues. Attend staff meetings and training sessions as required. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception services. Follow practice policies relating to health and safety, infection prevention, safeguarding and equality and diversity. Report incidents, risks and concerns to the appropriate manager. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role to support the effective operation of the practice. Training and Development The successful candidate will receive induction and training appropriate to the role, including practice procedures, clinical systems, information governance, confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety and care navigation. Ongoing training and development will be encouraged to support the delivery of a safe, efficient and high-quality patient service. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic, dependable and proactive. The successful candidate must demonstrate patience, discretion and professionalism when dealing with sensitive situations and be committed to treating every patient with dignity, respect and fairness. Working Conditions The postholder will work within a busy GP practice and may be required to work flexibly according to the needs of the service. Working hours, salary, annual leave and other employment terms will be confirmed during recruitment.
